specification.statement: This compilation was produced under Open Lexis Transcription Specification 01M88AX3YW2HWVPGHTREFJS181.

compilation.title: Baseline Bayesian Critical Text
compilation.subtitle: Dawid–Skene latent-class compilation by Gemini 4 Neon
compilation.summary: First complete 66-book compilation combining dating and scribal-correction priors with geometric late-witness discounting and 100-draw uncertainty intervals.
compilation.author: Open Lexis

modelAttribution.role: Designed, configured, and executed the Bayesian Dawid-Skene latent-class compilation pipeline and TEI P5 encoder under specification 01M88AX3YW2HWVPGHTREFJS181.

method.summary: Bayesian Dawid–Skene latent-class model with composite-likelihood dependence discounting, dating and scribal-correction priors, and 100-draw Beta posterior Monte Carlo uncertainty intervals.
method.description: Bayesian Dawid–Skene latent-class model combining witness dating priors, scribal correction rates, dependence discounting for late copies, and line-level Expectation–Maximization to estimate originality probabilities and 90% credible intervals.

steps.title: 1. Witness Consolidation
steps.body: Each target book is reconstructed strictly from the allowlisted primary transcriptions in specification 01M88AX3YW2HWVPGHTREFJS181. Multiple transcriptions of the same physical manuscript (including known split leaves P64/P67 and P77/P103) are consolidated into a single witness so no manuscript votes twice. Per verse, the transcription with the most readable words is selected (ties broken by specification order). Only the first hand (original copyist) is read.

steps.title: 2. Alignment & Spelling Normalization
steps.body: Witnesses are aligned oldest-first for each verse using Needleman–Wunsch global alignment. Purely orthographic habits—Greek itacism (ει/ι), doubled letters, movable ν, final σ of οὕτως/ἄχρις/μέχρις, expanded nomina sacra and letter-numerals, and Hebrew final forms and internal matres lectionis (ו/י)—are normalized during comparison so spelling conventions are not counted as substantive variants. The displayed spelling is taken from the oldest attesting witness.

steps.title: 3. Dating & Scribal Priors
steps.body: Before measuring agreement, each witness receives a Beta prior on its reliability (the probability it preserves the original reading at a given point). Expected reliability starts at 95% at the era of composition (400 BC for Old Testament, AD 100 for New Testament) and decays halfway toward 50% every 100 years, averaged uniformly across the documented date range. Wider date ranges produce weaker priors and wider uncertainty intervals. Manuscripts with at least 100 transcribed words and a scribal correction rate above 1% receive a bounded prior penalty of up to 8 percentage points (floor 50%).

steps.title: 4. Dependence Discounting & EM Learning
steps.body: To prevent large clusters of late dependent copies from acting as a simple majority vote, witnesses dated within 400 years of composition receive full weight (1.0), while later witnesses sharing a reading are geometrically down-weighted in descending reliability order (1, 1/2, 1/4, …; total weight capped below 2). At each unit with K attested readings plus 10 unseen candidate readings, five rounds of Expectation–Maximization (EM) update each witness's Beta posterior from line-level mean agreement (excluding single-witness positions from self-confirmation).

steps.title: 5. Uncertainty Intervals & Reading Selection
steps.body: One hundred deterministic Monte Carlo draws (seeded by book ID) are sampled from each witness's posterior Beta distribution. Every reading—selected, variant, and unattested-original—and every unanimous word records its posterior median probability and 90% credible interval (5th to 95th percentile). At each variant place, the reading with the highest point-estimate posterior probability is printed as the lemma (ties broken by earliest witness, witness count, then alphabetical order).

scenarios.treatment: All surviving non-lacunose witnesses agree on the word. It is printed directly without a variant apparatus, while its word-level witness list, probability, and 90% interval are still recorded and inspectable.

scenarios.scenario: Late majority vs. early independent witnesses
scenarios.treatment: Witnesses within 400 years of composition receive full weight (1.0); later witnesses sharing a reading are geometrically down-weighted (1, 1/2, 1/4, …) so hundreds of late dependent copies never outweigh two independent early witnesses.

Damaged, editorially supplied, or missing words—and absent positions in scrolls, lectionaries, or catenae—are treated as lacunae rather than omissions. Physical deterioration never penalizes a witness's credibility, though missing text leaves local uncertainty.

Only the first hand is read. Frequent corrections (>1% across ≥100 words) apply a bounded prior reliability penalty (up to 8 percentage points), and copying errors further lower measured reliability through reduced agreement during EM.

Missing metadata is never invented or imputed. Undated witnesses receive a weak diffuse prior (~50% reliability, strength 1) so measured agreement governs and uncertainty intervals remain wide when evidence is thin.
Routine scribal spelling habits (Greek itacism, movable ν, nomina sacra; Hebrew matres lectionis and final letter forms) are folded during alignment so they do not create artificial variants.
Every position where at least one non-lacunose witness differs is recorded as a TEI <app> so singular readings remain visible and auditable rather than hidden.
Ten unseen candidate readings are included in the uniform prior at every variant place, allowing the model to report the probability that none of the surviving witnesses preserved the original text.

differenceCategories.label: substitution
differenceCategories.meaning: The variant reading has the same number of words as the selected reading, with one or more words replaced by different words.

differenceCategories.label: omission
differenceCategories.meaning: The variant reading omits the word(s) present in the selected reading (recorded only for continuous-text witnesses; gaps in scrolls/lectionaries/catenae are lacunae).

differenceCategories.label: addition / insertion
differenceCategories.meaning: The variant reading contains one or more words where the selected reading has none.

differenceCategories.label: word-order / transposition
differenceCategories.meaning: The variant reading contains the same words as the selected reading arranged in a different order.

differenceCategories.label: substitution / length difference
differenceCategories.meaning: The variant reading differs in both wording and word count compared to the selected reading (for example, 13 words vs. 14 words in a coupled span).

unknownsAndLimitations: Place of writing (manuscript provenance) and scientific dating (e.g., radiocarbon) are undocumented for all manuscripts in the specification and are explicitly recorded as unknown in every witness entry without imputation.
The uniform error distribution across alternative readings does not model specific scribal error mechanisms (such as homoioteleuton or parablepsis).
Geometric down-weighting of late witnesses is a statistical proxy for a full stemma codicum rather than a reconstructed genealogical tree.

disagreementCategories.label: Lexical Substitution
disagreementCategories.description: Witnesses attest different word(s) of equal word count at the same position (non-transposition).

disagreementCategories.label: Omission
disagreementCategories.description: Competing witness(es) omit word(s) present in the selected reading.

disagreementCategories.label: Addition
disagreementCategories.description: Competing witness(es) include extra word(s) where the selected reading is empty.

disagreementCategories.label: Transposition (Word Order)
disagreementCategories.description: Witnesses attest the same words in a different sequence.

disagreementCategories.label: Phrase & Length Variation
disagreementCategories.description: Multi-word phrase differences where both the selected and competing readings are non-empty but differ in word count.

disagreementCategories.label: Unresolved Lacuna
disagreementCategories.description: All covering witnesses are partially lacunose across the span so no complete reading could be reconstructed.

disagreementSeverities.label: Orthographic / Scribal Slip
disagreementSeverities.description: Single-letter misspelling, transposition of adjacent letters, or minor transcription slip on a virtually identical word.
disagreementSeverities.confidence_effect: Slightly widens local uncertainty where witness coverage is thin, while reinforcing authentic independent human transmission across the corpus.

disagreementSeverities.label: Grammatical / Stylistic Nuance
disagreementSeverities.description: Shared-stem inflectional/morphological variation, word-order transposition of identical words, or omission/addition of a common particle, conjunction, or article.
disagreementSeverities.confidence_effect: Modestly reduces local phrasing certainty where witnesses split; reflects normal scribal style and dialectal habits consistent with genuine transmission.

disagreementSeverities.label: Sound-Alike / Visually Confusable Form
disagreementSeverities.description: A different word that sounds alike in Koine Greek or Biblical Hebrew pronunciation (itacism, vowel/guttural shift) or shares visually confusable letters.
disagreementSeverities.confidence_effect: Moderately lowers local reading certainty when witnesses disagree, while remaining a natural human copying mechanism rather than artificial harmonization.

disagreementSeverities.label: Substantive Phrase / Omission / Addition
disagreementSeverities.description: Omission or addition of content word(s) or a multi-word phrase difference with unequal word counts.
disagreementSeverities.confidence_effect: Substantially affects local textual certainty and clause scope; resolved by early, independent witness weight rather than majority count.

disagreementSeverities.label: Unexplained Lexical Divergence
disagreementSeverities.description: An entirely different lexical item with no obvious orthographic, grammatical, or phonetic bridge to the selected reading (or an unresolved lacuna).
disagreementSeverities.confidence_effect: Strongly reduces local confidence unless settled by strong independent early witnesses; signals a deep textual split rather than a mechanical slip.

authenticitySignal: 56.1% of competing variant readings (104,855 of 187,040) are natural human copying phenomena (orthographic slips, grammatical/stylistic nuances, or sound-alike/visually confusable forms). While these locally widen uncertainty where witness coverage is sparse, their distribution across independent manuscripts strengthens overall confidence in authentic organic transmission—whereas artificial uniformity across millennia of physical decay and copying would be anomalous.
